clue.text: Cap-badge to be proud of

parts.note: the idiom of an achievement worn as a plume in one's hat, read literally as an emblem on a cap

explanation.surface: Someone admires the badge on their regimental cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plume worn in a hat is the literal source of the idiom for a proud achievement.

clue.text: Aristophanes in a rubber suit?

parts.note: Aristophanes wrote the comedy The Frogs, and a diver in a wetsuit is named after that amphibian

explanation.surface: Picturing the Greek playwright wearing a rubber outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwater swimmer in a wetsuit is nicknamed after an amphibian, the subject of Aristophanes' play.

clue.text: Spinner of Noachian descent?

parts.note: His surname reads as a builder of Noah's vessel

explanation.surface: Asking about a cotton spinner descended from Noah.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Arkwright was an eighteenth-century English inventor of the water-powered spinning frame; his name splits as a maker of the ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The textile pioneer whose surname names a craftsman of Noah's boat.

clue.text: Barbarian to get honourable distinction ? What a notion !

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders
CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order of distinction

explanation.surface: A savage being honoured: what an idea!
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an intuitive feeling or suspicion, a guess.

clue.text: Pussyfoot under canvas

parts.note: Pussyfoot Johnson was a famous teetotal campaigner; the biblical tribe sworn off wine lived in tents

explanation.surface: A cat-footed prowler camping out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pussyfoot' (after the American prohibitionist W. E. Johnson) means a teetotaller; the descendants of Jonadab in Jeremiah drank no wine and dwelt in tents.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the abstinent biblical clan, or of the temperance society named after it, is a teetotaller.

clue.text: Gol ! What a load of work !

parts.note: the printed word is a three-letter log written the other way round, so it is a log back

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay at a heap of tasks waiting to be done.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Gol', not 'Go': GOL is LOG reversed, so the clue word is a log back.
explanation.definitionFit: Accumulated tasks still waiting to be dealt with form a heap of arrears.

clue.text: Sounded by Trumpeter Knox

parts.note: John Knox wrote The First ... of the Trumpet against the Monstrous Regiment of Women

explanation.surface: A bugle call played by a trumpeter called Knox.
explanation.walkthrough: John Knox was the sixteenth-century Scottish reformer whose tract against female rulers is titled as a trumpet's first sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud note on a horn, and the noun in the title of the reformer's pamphlet.

clue.text: Casts out of island those old initial intriguers

indicators.note: out of places the casts on the outside of the island

parts.note: taken as written
Bali is an Indonesian island

explanation.surface: Throwing people off an island: those old plotters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cabal was Charles II's ministry whose initials (Clifford, Arlington, Buckingham, Ashley, Lauderdale) spelt the word, hence 'initial intriguers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a secret clique of plotters, named after Charles II's acronymic ministry.

clue.text: Slate loose ? Only a tiny one !

indicators.note: loose signals that the letters of slate come apart and are reassembled

explanation.surface: A roof slate has come loose, but only a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest amount possible is the minimum, a tiny one.

clue.text: " Hesperus entreats thy light, —— excellently bright " (Jonson)

definitions.text: Hesperus entreats thy light, —— excellently bright " (Jonson)

parts.words: Hesperus entreats thy light, —— excellently bright
parts.note: a line from Ben Jonson's Hymn to Diana with its word of address removed, the title given to the moon deity

explanation.surface: A quotation from Ben Jonson's song to the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonson's Hymn to Diana, 'Queen and huntress, chaste and fair', addresses the moon as a female deity, 'excellently bright'.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana, the huntress and moon, is addressed as a female deity in Jonson's poem.

clue.text: " He comes the third time home with the —— garland " (Coriolanus)

definitions.text: He comes the third time home with the —— garland " (Coriolanus)

parts.words: He comes the third time home with the —— garland
parts.note: a line from Shakespeare's Coriolanus with one word left out; the missing adjective describes the victor's wreath of leaves

explanation.surface: A quotation about a Roman hero returning in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver fills the gap in the quotation; Romans awarded a crown of oak leaves for saving a citizen's life.
explanation.definitionFit: The civic crown awarded to Coriolanus was woven from leaves of the oak tree, so the garland is made of that wood's foliage.

clue.text: Applaud the bosses in the building line ?

parts.note: to applaud is to clap
a company's bosses form the board of directors

explanation.surface: Cheering the company directors in the construction trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlapping timber weatherboarding used to clad houses is a construction material.

clue.text: When to be in England for the ceremony ?

definitions.text: When to be in England for the ceremony ?

parts.words: When to be in England for the ceremony
parts.note: Browning's 'Oh, to be in England now that April's there' implies the time when the third month has gone by; also a military parade

explanation.surface: Asking at what time of year to visit England for a ceremonial occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning wished to be in England in April, that is, once the third month has passed; the two words together are also a parade of troops past a saluting point.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal parade of troops filing by a reviewing officer is a military ceremony.

clue.text: Illuminated, he becomes supple

parts.note: illuminated means lit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man lit up turns flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a body that bends easily and gracefully.

clue.text: Tennyson's black bat

parts.note: Tennyson's Maud has the line 'the black bat, ..., has flown', naming the bat as the hours of darkness

explanation.surface: A creature that appears in a Victorian poet's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Tennyson's Maud the black bat is a metaphor for the dark hours, which have flown when dawn comes.

clue.text: Produced a brain-child with increased concentration

definitions.text: Produced a brain-child with increased concentration

parts.words: Produced a brain-child with increased concentration
parts.note: invented an idea, with the second word suggesting thinking intensified, turned upwards

explanation.surface: Someone concentrated harder and came up with a new idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent or devise an idea is to conceive it in the mind.

clue.text: "And treat those two —— just the same " (Kipling)

definitions.text: "And treat those two —— just the same " (Kipling)

parts.words: And treat those two —— just the same
parts.note: a line from Kipling's poem If with its noun removed; it calls Triumph and Disaster a pair of frauds

explanation.surface: A line of Kipling's advice about meeting good and bad fortune alike.
explanation.walkthrough: In If, Kipling writes of meeting Triumph and Disaster 'And treat those two impostors just the same'; the gap takes that noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling calls Triumph and Disaster deceivers, people pretending to be what they are not.

clue.text: Sweet-smelling apples ?

parts.note: the name comes from French pomme d'ambre, apple of amber, a perfumed ball

explanation.surface: A question about fragrant fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls of perfume or spice-studded oranges, named from French for apple of amber.

clue.text: Does it give extra horse-power to the boat ?

definitions.text: Does it give extra horse-power to the boat ?

parts.words: Does it give extra horse-power to the boat
parts.note: the word is both a float projecting from a canoe and a horse harnessed alongside the shafts

explanation.surface: Asking whether some device makes a boat go faster.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting float steadies a canoe, and the same word names an extra horse harnessed outside the shafts.

clue.text: Moving spirit ?

parts.note: a moving spirit is normally a leading person, but here it is the fuel spirit that moves vehicles

explanation.surface: Asking who is the driving force behind an enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil refined into motor spirit is the fuel that drives engines.

clue.text: Demonstrably fell heavily for the candidate !

definitions.text: Demonstrably fell heavily for the candidate !

parts.words: Demonstrably fell heavily for the candidate
parts.note: to drop down heavily, and to give one's vote firmly to a single candidate

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled openly for a political candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to sit down heavily and to vote decisively for one choice.

clue.text: Notes returned for stitching

indicators.note: returned says the word notes is read from its last letter back to its first

explanation.surface: Messages sent back about some sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: In surgery this is a thread drawn through the skin to keep a wound draining, a kind of suture.

clue.text: Upraised firearm secures gold pieces

indicators.note: upraised in a down clue lifts the weapon's letters so they read bottom to top

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
to secure something is to get it

explanation.surface: A raised rifle protects the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumps of native gold found by prospectors.

clue.text: Consumer's employment

parts.note: what a consumer does with goods, and also employment in the sense of putting something to use

explanation.surface: A remark about the job held by a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Employing a thing means putting it to use, which is what a consumer does with what they buy.

clue.text: I am getting on to one hundred in orderly fashion

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I
the Roman numeral for a hundred is C

explanation.surface: Someone getting on for a hundred years old behaves tidily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In orderly fashion' means in the style of one of the classical orders of architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek architectural order with scroll capitals is one of the classical orders.

clue.text: After this chaff is out, presumably !

definitions.text: After this chaff is out, presumably !

parts.words: After this chaff is out, presumably
parts.note: chaff here is husks separated from grain, not teasing banter, and this is the process that blows it away

explanation.surface: A remark that the joking and banter will be over afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers toss threshed grain in a draught so the light husks blow away, leaving clean grain.

clue.text: What Henley did not do in the fell clutch of circumstance

definitions.text: What Henley did not do in the fell clutch of circumstance

parts.words: What Henley did not do in the fell clutch of circumstance
parts.note: W. E. Henley's poem Invictus says 'In the fell clutch of circumstance I have not ... nor cried aloud'

explanation.surface: A reference to the defiant poet's response to hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: In Invictus Henley says he did not flinch in pain under misfortune.

clue.text: One should do nothing vulgar !

definitions.meaning: a colloquial, uneducated form of nought, meaning zero

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid anything coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: The modal of obligation, and a dialect spelling of zero.

clue.text: One and ten in coppers; a sorry affair

indicators.note: in puts the one and ten inside the coins named by coppers

parts.note: British copper coins are pence
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eleven in small change; a contrite feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sorry for one's wrongdoing is contrition, a state of repentance.

clue.text: Dance in the old suite

parts.note: the baroque suite of dances usually ended with a lively jig movement of French name

explanation.surface: A dance performed in a set of rooms from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively baroque movement in compound time closed the classical dance suite.

clue.text: Tenfold

parts.note: the single word is a plain definition: multiplied by a factor of ten

explanation.definitionFit: Both mean multiplied by ten, from Latin decem.

clue.text: Resist a show of lampoons

indicators.note: a show of the letters here is a rearranged display of them, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Withstand a display of mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampoons are pieces of mocking ridicule, works that hold people up to scorn.
